findings.problem: Nine handlers read run_id or artifact_id with RequiredInt and then convert with int64(runIDInt). params.go now has requiredInt64 for GitHub database IDs, which can be larger than 32 bits. Going through int adds a step that is not needed.
findings.fix: Change each `runIDInt, err := RequiredInt(request, "run_id")` / `runID := int64(runIDInt)` pair to `runID, err := requiredInt64(request, "run_id")`. The lines are 356, 412, 483, 823, 886, 949, 1013, 1147 and 1210. Do the same for artifact_id at line 1081.

findings.problem: GetJobLogs reads job_id and run_id with OptionalIntParam and then casts them with int64(jobID) and int64(runID) when it calls handleFailedJobLogs and handleSingleJobLogs. optionalInt64Param already does this.
findings.fix: Use optionalInt64Param for job_id and run_id, and remove the int64(...) casts at the call sites.

findings.problem: Only pagination_test.go uses WithUnifiedPagination and PaginationParams.ToGraphQLParams (line 107). All GraphQL tools use WithCursorPagination with CursorPaginationParams. These functions add public API that no code calls.
findings.fix: Delete WithUnifiedPagination and PaginationParams.ToGraphQLParams, along with their cases in TestPaginationToolOptions and the "rest/" subtests in TestToGraphQLParams. Add them back when a tool needs them.

findings.problem: OptionalPaginationParams now also reads "after". It is used only by REST tools, and WithPagination does not declare "after" for them. So PaginationParams.After is always empty in real calls, and a stray "after" argument can still make a REST tool fail with a type error.
findings.fix: Remove the After field and the "after" lookup from PaginationParams and OptionalPaginationParams. Cursor tools already use OptionalCursorPaginationParams.

findings.problem: The REST default page size is the literal 30 here and again in sub_issues.go:57. The GraphQL default has a named constant, DefaultGraphQLPageSize.
findings.fix: Add `DefaultRESTPageSize = 30` next to DefaultGraphQLPageSize. Use it in OptionalPaginationParams and in ListSubIssues.

findings.problem: ListCommits has a dead fallback, `if perPage == 0 { perPage = 30 }`. OptionalPaginationParams already returns 30 when perPage is 0 or missing.
findings.fix: Remove the perPage local and the if block, and pass pagination.PerPage directly.

findings.problem: ListIssues reads page and perPage with raw type assertions on request.GetArguments(). A wrong type is silently ignored, and the defaults differ from every other WithPagination tool.
findings.fix: Call OptionalPaginationParams(request), return a tool error on failure, and set opts.ListOptions = github.ListOptions{Page: pagination.Page, PerPage: pagination.PerPage}.

findings.problem: The pageInfoOutput test type copies pageInfoResult from pagination.go field for field, including the JSON tags.
findings.fix: Delete pageInfoOutput and use pageInfoResult in the test table and in the unmarshal targets.

findings.problem: discussions.go writes the owner and repo descriptions as "Repository owner" and "Repository name" string literals. actions.go defines the DescriptionRepositoryOwner and DescriptionRepositoryName constants for these, but no other file uses them.
findings.fix: Move the constants to a shared file such as params.go, and use them in discussions.go and sub_issues.go (withSubIssueParentParams). If they will not be shared, remove them.

findings.problem: ListSubIssues declares owner, repo and issue_number inline, while the other three sub-issue tools use withSubIssueParentParams. The only difference is the issue_number description.
findings.fix: Use withSubIssueParentParams() in ListSubIssues as well, and update its toolsnap. If the different description is needed, give the helper a description argument.

findings.problem: userOrOrgHandler sets TotalCount and IncompleteResults from result.GetTotal() and result.GetIncompleteResults(), then sets them again from the pointers in two if blocks. The second assignment changes nothing.
findings.fix: Delete the `if result.Total != nil` and `if result.IncompleteResults != nil` blocks.

findings.problem: The comment says the sort defaults to "created", but the code passes the user's sort value unchanged, and GitHub's default is best match.
getErrorResult does not call t.Helper(), unlike the helpers around it. A failed assertion is reported at the helper's line, not at the test that called it.
findings.fix: Add t.Helper() as the first statement of getErrorResult.

The two GraphQL call sites (discussions.go:177 and :324) use OptionalCursorPaginationParams and CursorPaginationParams.ToGraphQLParams. Deleting these also makes finding 3 simpler, because this ToGraphQLParams is the only code that reads PaginationParams.After.

kept.problem: OptionalPaginationParams now also reads "after". It is used only by REST tools, and WithPagination does not declare "after" for them. So PaginationParams.After is always empty in real calls, and a stray "after" argument can still make a REST tool fail with a type error.
kept.fix: Remove the After field and the "after" lookup from PaginationParams and OptionalPaginationParams. Cursor tools already use OptionalCursorPaginationParams.
kept.why: Confirmed. All callers of OptionalPaginationParams are REST tools declared with WithPagination, which has only page and perPage. No production code reads PaginationParams.After. Because OptionalPaginationParams still parses "after", a stray non-string "after" argument makes a REST tool return a type error.

kept.why: Confirmed. The REST default 30 is written as a literal in OptionalPaginationParams (pagination.go:89) and again in sub_issues.go:57. The GraphQL default of the same value has a named constant, DefaultGraphQLPageSize. A DefaultRESTPageSize constant would give one source for the REST default.

kept.problem: ListCommits has a dead fallback, `if perPage == 0 { perPage = 30 }`. OptionalPaginationParams already returns 30 when perPage is 0 or missing.
kept.fix: Remove the perPage local and the if block, and pass pagination.PerPage directly.
kept.why: Confirmed. OptionalIntParamWithDefault returns the default 30 whenever the value is 0 or missing. So the `if perPage == 0 { perPage = 30 }` block in ListCommits never runs.

kept.problem: ListIssues reads page and perPage with raw type assertions on request.GetArguments(). A wrong type is silently ignored, and the defaults differ from every other WithPagination tool.
kept.fix: Call OptionalPaginationParams(request), return a tool error on failure, and set opts.ListOptions = github.ListOptions{Page: pagination.Page, PerPage: pagination.PerPage}.
kept.why: Confirmed. ListIssues declares WithPagination but reads page and perPage with raw `.(float64)` assertions. It repeats what OptionalPaginationParams does, but a wrong type is silently dropped instead of returning a tool error. When the values are missing it sends 0 instead of the usual 1/30.
